site.name: Akhil Patil
site.title: Akhil Patil — Marketing Analytics & Causal Measurement
site.authorRole: Senior Marketing Analyst, Plymouth Rock Assurance
site.blogTagline: Essays on causal measurement, media analytics, and building the data machinery behind marketing decisions.
site.blogDescription: Long-form essays on incrementality testing, geo holdout experiments, media analytics, and applied machine learning — by Akhil Patil, Sr. Marketing Analyst.

incrementality-testing.label: Incrementality Testing
incrementality-testing.title: Incrementality Testing & Causal Measurement
incrementality-testing.seoDescription: Field notes on incrementality testing for marketing — geo holdout design, synthetic control groups, difference-in-differences readouts, and power analysis.
incrementality-testing.intro: Attribution tells you what got clicked. Incrementality tells you what actually changed behaviour. These essays cover the full experimental stack I use to answer the only media question that matters — if we turned this channel off, what would we actually lose? — including geo holdout design, synthetic control construction, Mahalanobis matching, power analysis and minimum detectable effect sizing, difference-in-differences measurement, and the discipline of being honest about what a test can and cannot prove.

media-strategy.label: Media Strategy
media-strategy.title: Media Strategy & Geo Targeting
media-strategy.seoDescription: How to decide where marketing budget works hardest — market opportunity indices, weighted zip-code targeting frameworks, and evidence-based vendor selection.
media-strategy.intro: Deciding where to spend is a harder analytical problem than deciding how much. A market can look efficient simply because it's saturated, or look expensive simply because it's under-penetrated. These essays cover the decision-support machinery I build for media teams: normalized opportunity indices that make hundreds of markets comparable on one axis, weighted ranking frameworks for sub-market geo targeting, and significance testing to settle vendor and device questions with evidence instead of habit.

data-machinery.label: Data Machinery
data-machinery.title: Data Machinery & Operational Analytics
data-machinery.seoDescription: The foundations of marketing analytics — entity resolution across fragmented systems, funnel opportunity sizing, and KPI alerting people actually trust.
data-machinery.intro: Most analytics failures are not modelling failures. They are foundation failures: the same customer counted three times across three systems, a funnel nobody can measure end to end, an alert nobody trusts because it cried wolf. These essays are about the unglamorous machinery underneath the insight — entity resolution across systems with no shared key, prospect-level datasets that make a real funnel measurable, automated cross-sell views, and statistical process control that fires when something is genuinely wrong.

applied-ml.label: Applied ML
applied-ml.title: Applied Machine Learning
applied-ml.seoDescription: Applied machine learning for customer analytics — K-means and PCA segmentation, churn prediction with LDA topic modeling, and modeling value without labels.
applied-ml.intro: A model that scores well and changes nothing is a failed project. These essays are about applied machine learning where the constraint is rarely the algorithm — it is sparse labels, unstructured text, selection bias, and the gap between a prediction and an action someone can actually take. Topics include K-means segmentation rescued by principal component analysis, churn prediction paired with LDA topic modeling of call-center notes, and the honest engineering required when under two percent of your population has a usable label.
